items.item: Every status column heading shows the status name and its ticket count, and the count equals the cards shown or the column states how many are not shown (such as "Showing 20 of 134")
items.evidence: renderBoard() in page.html: `var countEl = h("span", {...}, overLimit ? "Over limit" : countText);` — when the 'In progress' column exceeds its limit (7 tickets vs status.limit:6), the header replaces the numeric count with the text "Over limit" (visible in first.png), so no count or 'X of Y' figure is shown for that column even though all 7 cards are still rendered below it.

items.item: Each card shows the ticket number (such as #4821), subject, customer, priority as a word or code (such as "P1 · Urgent") and the assignee, or an explicit "Unassigned"
items.evidence: makeCard(): topRow shows `ticket.id` (e.g. "TK-1050") and priorityLabel() (word, e.g. "Urgent"); title shows subject; customerLine shows `ticket.customer.name + ' · ' + ticket.customer.company`; metaRow shows avatar+assignee name or the literal text "Unassigned" when `!ticket.assignee`.

items.item: Open tickets show the time left to the next SLA target and which target it is (such as "Resolution due in 2h 15m"), and breached tickets show how long they are overdue (such as "Breached 40m ago") in text or with an icon, not by colour alone
items.evidence: dueInfo() only ever produces generic strings like "Due 07/11 · in 4h" or "Due 06/11 · overdue 16h" / badge "Overdue 16h" — there is a single undifferentiated `dueAt` per ticket and no label naming which SLA target (first response vs resolution) the countdown refers to, so 'which target it is' is never communicated.

items.item: Tickets in a waiting status (such as "Waiting on customer") show their SLA timer as paused instead of counting down
items.evidence: dueInfo() has no branch for status 'waiting' — waiting tickets (e.g. TK-1034) go through the same `diffMs = ticket.dueAt - NOW` logic as any open ticket and render "Due 08/11 · in 1 day" with no 'Paused' label or icon.

items.item: Within each column the cards are ordered by SLA due time or by priority, and the board states which ordering is used
items.evidence: colTickets.sort(function(a,b){ return sortRank(a) - sortRank(b); }) does order by due/resolved/closed time, but no column header or UI text anywhere states the ordering rule (no 'Sorted by due date' or similar label in the header markup around line 577-592).

items.item: Search finds tickets by number, subject or customer, and filters cover assignee (including "Me" and "Unassigned"), priority and SLA state (such as breached or due within 1 hour)
items.evidence: applyFilters(): search only checks `t.id` and `t.subject` ('if (t.id...indexOf(q)===-1 && t.subject...indexOf(q)===-1) return false'), never `t.customer.name`; filters exist for assignee (incl. '__unassigned__' option and 'Assigned to me' checkbox) and priority, but there is no filter control for SLA state (breached / due within 1h) anywhere in the toolbar markup.

items.item: Each card has keyboard-reachable actions to assign the ticket (including "Assign to me") and to change its status without dragging, with accessible names that include the ticket number
items.evidence: The kebab button (`aria-label: "Actions for " + ticket.id`) opens moveMenuFor() with 'Move to…' status options (no drag needed, accessible name includes ticket number) — satisfies the status-change half, but there is no 'Assign' or 'Assign to me' action anywhere on the card or its menu; assignment is only possible via the `#panel-assignee` select inside the detail side panel.

items.item: An empty column shows a short message instead of blank space, a search or filter with no matches offers to clear it, and loading and failed-load (with retry) states exist
items.evidence: renderBoard(): empty column renders `h("li", ...) 'No tickets in ' + status.label.toLowerCase()`; `#state-no-results` shows "No tickets match these filters" with a "Clear filters" button; `renderSkeleton()` provides a loading skeleton; `#state-error` shows "Couldn't load tickets" with a `#btn-retry` button.

items.item: Every relative time (such as "Updated 3h ago") also exposes the exact date, time and timezone, in a <time datetime> element or a title attribute
items.evidence: No `<time>` element exists anywhere in page.html and only two `title` attributes exist in the whole file (the blocked-close-menu tooltip and the card's `title: ticket.id + ' — ' + ticket.subject`). Relative strings like "in 4h", "Overdue 16h", "Due soon" (dueInfo()) and activity timestamps (fmtDateTime(), only dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm, no timezone) carry no exact-timestamp exposure via datetime or title.

notes: tracked-uppercase-labels evidence: detail panel section headers repeatedly use `class: "text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-wide text-slate-400"` for 'Customer', 'Description', 'Assignee', 'SLA', 'Move to', 'Resolution note', 'Activity' (openDetailPanel(), lines ~756-827). No other template tells observed: no gradients, no backdrop-blur/glass, no oversized radii (only rounded-md/rounded-full, radii 4-6px per audit.json), no greeting header, no KPI tiles, no delta pills, no decorative charts, no sidebar promo, no navy/indigo sidebar (no sidebar at all), avatars show initials only for real assigned agents (legitimate use, not flagged). Automated audit.json flags 5 text-contrast failures (2.56:1) on the 'Unassigned' label text in cards and 1 font-size-base violation on #summary-line (12px); these are accessibility/visual issues outside the checklist scope but worth noting.
